Water, Industry Groups Praise Overwhelming 415-9 House Passage of WRDA Bill

By Esther D'Amico
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:14
Instaread
September 22, 2026

Industry and water groups praised overwhelming passage by the U.S. House last week of the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) and urged a bipartisan effort in both chambers to finalize the water infrastructure legislation this session.

The biennial legislation that authorizes flood risk management, navigation and ecosystem restoration projects for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers passed House legislators on Sept. 16 by a noteworthy 415-9 vote. In July, the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee unanimously advanced its own WRDA legislation to the full Senate, where it is still awaiting a full floor vote.

Before the legislation can be sent for presidential consideration, the House and Senate would need to reconcile differences between their bills.

There’s strong bipartisan support in both chambers for reconciling the two bills, Charlotte Mitchell Duyshart, associate legislative director of the National Association of Counties, told ENR. 

“I’ve had a bunch of meetings with congressional staff ... in the last couple of weeks, and it seems like the enthusiasm is there on both sides for sure,” she said. Conference negotiations for the House-passed bill and the Senate committee version appear to be under way, she said.

“WRDA is historically a very bipartisan thing that everyone wants to get done because everyone has an Army Corps project in their district or state that they want some funding for a new feasibility study for,” Duyshart said.

It is likely a WRDA bill will be one of the few items Congress passes in the lame duck session, but it may be attached to other legislation such as defense authorization or appropriations bills, she said.

The House bill would authorize 133 new feasibility studies for locally proposed water resources infrastructure projects and 14 projects already vetted by the Corps and ready for Congress to authorize construction. The legislation would include policy changes aimed to improve water infrastructure project delivery, such as reauthorized alternative project delivery programs, and emphasizes input from non-federal interests for feasibility studies.

The House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee said the bill includes policies that will improve non-federal interests’ ability to obtain valuable technical assistance and to fund construction more quickly, as well as to encourage the Corps to increase use of multi-year contracts.

“WRDA 2026 makes significant improvements across the country to our inland waterways, ports and harbors, flood protection and other critical water infrastructure,” said committee Chair Sam Graves (R-MO). “This bill also makes common-sense reforms to the Army Corps of Engineers’ policies, empowers local communities and expedites project delivery.”

The Senate bill authorizes 61 feasibility studies and 15 new or modified construction projects nationwide, as well as U.S. Environmental Protection Agency drinking water and wastewater infrastructure programs, including State Revolving Funds (SRF), and increases in authorized funding levels.

The biggest differences between the bills is the Senate’s inclusion of SRF program reauthorization, which is absent from the House version, Duyshart said. The SRF program is important because it provides below-market financing for water infrastructure projects, which is especially critical for smaller and more rural counties that have difficulties raising revenue, she said. 

While the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) provides supplemental and advanced appropriations for SRF programs, the IIJA expires on September 30. The SRF programs need reauthorization so their federal funding does not dry up, she said.

“We’re hoping to see the SRF numbers in a final version of the WRDA bill, however, [it ultimately] comes together,” Duyshart said.

Several groups, including the National Utility Contractors Association (NUCA), favor the Senate’s more comprehensive bill over the House legislation. 

The group urges the House to reconcile its bill with the Senate version, which would extend the critical SRFs for four years and increase resources. The Senate bill would also support lead service line replacement and PFAS removal as well as investing in workforce development, cybersecurity, resilience and other infrastructure improvements, said Zack Perconti, NUCA's vice president and chief advocacy officer.

“During the upcoming lame-duck session, NUCA will continue to urge Congress to pass comprehensive water infrastructure legislation that addresses the many unfulfilled demands to improve the nation's waterways, drinking water and wastewater infrastructure,” he said in a statement.

KEYWORDS: House legislation US Army Corps of Engineers water resources development act WRDA
